pages.text: A mixture carried down a packed column comes apart: each part sticks to the packing for its own time. The bands spread as they go - the $(thing)plate height H = A + B/u + C·u$() (van Deemter) is smallest at a middling flow - and two parts come out clean when the resolution $(thing)Rs$() reaches 1.5.

The $(item)Chromatography Column$() is a tower: every storey adds a metre of column and more plates, for harder splits. Set the carrier flow and the oven temperature. It splits $(fluid)Molecular Cloud$() gas into water and ammonia, methane and hydrogen cyanide, and the dust clouds' medium into $(item)PAH Soot$().

Gases that come off it pure are $(thing)assayed$(): Hydrogen, Nitrogen, Oxygen, Methane and Carbon Monoxide. From now on these, like the acids, poison a chemical catalyst when fed in unassayed (five runs each).
